prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create ONE standalone Kalistar character illustration, portrait 4:5 (ideally 1122 x 1402), edge-to-edge artwork. Absolutely no card frame, words, letters, logos, numbers, stats or UI. Match the supplied Momo and Valazar references: narrative hand-painted fantasy illustration, constructed colour planes, expressive believable anatomy, selective visible oil/gouache brushwork, lost-and-found edges, worn tactile materials, motivated light. Paint the face with colour planes too; no photographic pores, glossy CGI, manga/anime eyes, airbrushed beauty advertising, artificial depth-of-field blur or uniformly applied texture noise. Face and principal action readable in the central 60 percent width, important objects clear of the outer 10 percent, enough breathing room for a later 737 x 921 card illustration crop. The painting is a narrative instant, not a character posing for a camera.
Reference roles: image 1 Momo and image 2 Valazar define ONLY the Kalistar painted language and material handling. Image 3 Seraphina defines ONLY the existing VAMP species cues and Draevenheim's gothic material culture, NOT her face, gender or pose.
Subject: Baptiste, an adult male Vamp virtuoso violinist, elegant and quietly frightening, standing alone on a small stone dais giving a concert inside a Draevenheim gothic hall. A sharply tailored worn black-and-wine velvet long coat, understated aged silver clasps, ivory collar, a composed adult angular face with subtle pointed ears and one small hint of a canine in a restrained predatory smile, dark hair swept back with slightly silver temples. He is handsome through character and poise, not a smooth anime prince. Pale cool skin painted in solid brush planes. His expression holds dangerous concentration and enjoyment of the audience's held breath.
He is ACTIVELY PLAYING a real, physically coherent violin: the body supported between left shoulder and chin, left hand around the neck with fingers over the fingerboard, right hand gripping the frog of a single straight bow. Bow hair actually touches the strings between bridge and fingerboard at a believable angle. One complete violin with attached neck and scroll, four strings, bridge and tailpiece aligned. Both hands, the bow-to-string contact, and his face are cleanly separated and centrally readable. The bow is not fused with his arm or broken into several sticks. Exactly one head, two arms, two hands, two legs.
A few seated listeners at the far sides are subdued silhouettes, shoulders held tense; do not fill the background with detailed faces. Tall cool blue-grey pointed arches, a restrained burgundy curtain, candles casting warm light onto his cheek, hands and the amber violin. One fine dark-crimson resonance glows near the strings, HEMATO as musical menace, not gore, not huge magical ribbons. The concert feels alive and unsettling, refined rather than monstrous. Three-quarter nearly full-length framing, instrument and face much more prominent than the hall, no decorative poster pose, no writing, music notes or sheet-music text.
